fields.title: How to Choose the Right Laptop in 2026
fields.excerpt: From processor and RAM to display and battery, here is everything you need to know before buying your next laptop.
fields.content:
Choosing a laptop can feel overwhelming with so many options. Let's break it down into what actually matters.

First, decide your use case. For everyday tasks and browsing, an Intel Core i5 or equivalent with 8GB RAM and a 512GB SSD is plenty. For creative work or gaming, look at a Core i7/i9 with a dedicated GPU and 16GB+ RAM.

Display quality matters more than people think — a Full HD IPS panel is the minimum, while OLED offers stunning colour for creators. Finally, balance battery life against performance: ultrabooks last all day, while powerful machines trade battery for speed.

Visit any TechZone store for a free consultation and hands-on demo before you decide.

fields.title: iPhone 15 Pro Max Review: Titanium Done Right
fields.excerpt: We spent two weeks with the iPhone 15 Pro Max. Here is our honest take on the camera, performance and battery.
fields.content:
The iPhone 15 Pro Max is the most refined iPhone Apple has made. The switch to titanium makes it noticeably lighter, and the matte finish feels premium without being slippery.

The A17 Pro chip is blisteringly fast — console-quality games run beautifully. The 5x telephoto camera is the headline feature, delivering crisp zoomed shots that earlier iPhones simply couldn't.

Battery life comfortably lasts a full day of heavy use. The move to USB-C is long overdue and welcome. At its price, it's a significant investment, but for power users it's worth every rupee.

fields.title: 7 Ways to Extend Your Smartphone Battery Life
fields.excerpt: Simple, practical tips to make your phone last longer between charges — no apps required.
fields.content:
Battery anxiety is real, but a few habits can make a big difference.

1. Lower your screen brightness or use auto-brightness.
2. Enable dark mode on OLED screens.
3. Turn off background app refresh for apps you rarely use.
4. Disable always-on display if you don't need it.
5. Use Wi-Fi instead of mobile data when possible.
6. Keep your software updated for efficiency improvements.
7. Avoid extreme temperatures — heat is a battery killer.

Follow these and you'll easily squeeze extra hours out of every charge.

fields.title: OLED vs QLED: Which TV Technology Is Right for You?
fields.excerpt: The two leading TV technologies compared — picture quality, brightness, price and ideal use cases.
fields.content:
OLED and QLED are the two premium TV technologies, and they excel in different areas.

OLED panels produce perfect blacks because each pixel lights itself — ideal for dark rooms and movie lovers. QLED, on the other hand, gets much brighter, making it better for bright living rooms and HDR highlights.

For gaming, both now offer 120Hz and low latency. QLED tends to be more affordable at larger sizes, while OLED commands a premium for its contrast.

Our recommendation: choose OLED for cinematic viewing in controlled lighting, and QLED for bright rooms and value at large sizes.
